diagnostics: Weight-shard size comes from the pinned manifest; actual transferred bytes are not equated with artifact size.
Request first output is the first nonempty text chunk, not exact first-token time.

60 measured requests: 3 windows of 20 sequential requests, no added delay within windows, full 90-second loaded-idle gaps after responses 20 and 40. One separate warmup. 60-second request and 30-minute session safety limits; timeouts are incomplete, not successful results.

plan.resetPolicy: resetChat before every request; fixed prompt for repeats; seed 42

events.label: Page hidden; session continues under browser background policy

signals.label: Main-page JS heap
signals.reason: Nonstandard browser estimate, possibly rounded/shared; excludes worker and GPU.

signals.label: Main-page timer delay
signals.reason: Responsiveness, not CPU utilization. Delayed samples retain actual timestamps.

signals.label: Process CPU utilization
signals.reason: Exact process CPU percent requires an external OS/browser lab collector. Timer delay and CPU pressure are not CPU percent.

signals.label: Process RAM / physical GPU VRAM
signals.reason: Requires external process/GPU instrumentation; WebGPU buffer descriptors do not expose residency.

signals.label: Cross-context memory estimate
signals.reason: Cross-origin isolation is false; this API requires isolation and browser support.

signals.label: CPU pressure
signals.reason: Observed coarse system pressure. Not per-process usage and not a CPU percentage.

signals.label: Tracked live GPUBuffer sizes
signals.reason: Sum of buffer descriptor sizes not explicitly destroyed on this device. Includes runtime pool buffers; excludes textures, driver overhead and physical VRAM residency.

signals.label: GPU device lifecycle
signals.reason: Unexpected loss is a failed run; destroy during unload is an expected lifecycle event.

signals.label: Reachable WASM linear memory
signals.reason: Linear address-space length, not resident RAM; may remain reachable after unload. No forced GC.

signals.label: Worker JS heap
signals.reason: performance.memory is not exposed in this worker.

signals.label: Worker timer delay
signals.reason: Worker responsiveness; includes scheduling and synchronous work, not CPU usage.

network.note: Worker resource timings for this run. Positive transfer sizes are an observed lower bound only. Zero can mean cache or hidden cross-origin timing, not a verified zero-byte download.

clockAlignment.method: Shared host epoch, calibrated browser performance clock, monotonic native interval deltas
clockAlignment.notes: Browser phase/request times share the calibrated epoch. Power timestamps are line-buffered CLI header receipt times; delivery adds uncertainty. Native samples use actual timestamps, not assumed one-second spacing.

coverage.label: Browser process-tree CPU
coverage.source: libproc own CPU ticks → mach_timebase_info → interval delta
coverage.reason: RUSAGE_INFO CPU counters are Mach absolute ticks, converted using mach_timebase_info. Delta own user+system CPU nanoseconds / elapsed monotonic nanoseconds * 100. 100% = one logical CPU; capacity percent divides by logical CPU count. Child CPU totals are never added again. Incomplete process intervals are null in charts; raw partial values retained.

coverage.label: Accounted process footprint
coverage.reason: Footprint is the sum of per-process kernel-accounted phys_footprint values, not a globally deduplicated physical-memory measurement. RSS is retained per process and summed only as a labeled non-deduplicated statistic; shared pages may be counted repeatedly. Never add browser WASM/GPU buffer sizes to either OS metric.

coverage.label: GPU activity
coverage.reason: Driver-reported device activity across all applications; sampling window is driver-defined. Not benchmark-only GPU use.

coverage.label: Chrome GPU time (experimental)
coverage.reason: Driver-accounted command-buffer time for the dedicated Chrome process tree, including browser rendering. Approximate nanosecond accounting, not shader occupancy, reserved GPU cores, or model-only utilization. Concurrent queues may overlap, so time per second is not a capacity percentage. Undocumented Apple driver property: availability and semantics may change. Client/PID changes, queue changes, regressions and read failures create gaps. AppUsage has no stable queue identifiers; positional continuity checks are best effort.

coverage.label: Thermal pressure
coverage.reason: 0 nominal, 1 fair, 2 serious, 3 critical. This is pressure, not temperature in degrees.

coverage.label: Memory pressure and swap
coverage.reason: Host pressure level is a raw kernel category; swap is host-wide. Free pages are not total available/reclaimable memory.

coverage.label: Estimated CPU / GPU / ANE power
coverage.reason: Estimated subsystem power across all applications, never model watts. Energy integrates observed interval overlap only.

energy.scope: Host CPU+GPU+ANE subsystem estimate; not device wall power or model-attributed energy
energy.note: Five seconds of observed pre-run baseline when available. Integrate power over overlap with active time; missing intervals are not filled. Above-baseline energy is a host change, not causal attribution to the model.

collector.scope: Only the dedicated browser root PID and its observed descendants. Retain children across reparenting; PID + kernel start time prevents PID-reuse contamination. Dedicated workers run within renderer processes, not necessarily separate OS processes.
collector.cpuNormalization: RUSAGE_INFO CPU counters are Mach absolute ticks, converted using mach_timebase_info. Delta own user+system CPU nanoseconds / elapsed monotonic nanoseconds * 100. 100% = one logical CPU; capacity percent divides by logical CPU count. Child CPU totals are never added again.
collector.memorySemantics: Footprint is the sum of per-process kernel-accounted phys_footprint values, not a globally deduplicated physical-memory measurement. RSS is retained per process and summed only as a labeled non-deduplicated statistic; shared pages may be counted repeatedly. Never add browser WASM/GPU buffer sizes to either OS metric.
collector.hostScope: GPU activity, thermal state, pressure, swap and power describe the whole host; other applications remain running. No strict resource reservation or CPU/RAM caps.
collector.gaps: One-second process-tree snapshots can miss processes that are born and exit between polls. Newly observed and exited processes lack a complete interval; missing intervals are explicitly counted.
collector.kernelEnergySemantics: Raw ri_energy_nj counter retained for provenance only. Not used as model watts or substituted for powermetrics subsystem power.
collector.gpuTimeSemantics: Driver-accounted command-buffer time for the dedicated Chrome process tree, including browser rendering. Approximate nanosecond accounting, not shader occupancy, reserved GPU cores, or model-only utilization. Concurrent queues may overlap, so time per second is not a capacity percentage. Undocumented Apple driver property: availability and semantics may change. Client/PID changes, queue changes, regressions and read failures create gaps. AppUsage has no stable queue identifiers; positional continuity checks are best effort.

provenance.gpuTimeSemantics: Driver-accounted command-buffer time for the dedicated Chrome process tree, including browser rendering. Approximate nanosecond accounting, not shader occupancy, reserved GPU cores, or model-only utilization. Concurrent queues may overlap, so time per second is not a capacity percentage. Undocumented Apple driver property: availability and semantics may change. Client/PID changes, queue changes, regressions and read failures create gaps. AppUsage has no stable queue identifiers; positional continuity checks are best effort.

browserStorageCopy.note: Every chart point and interval is retained. Raw process snapshots, GPU counters and powermetrics text remain in the hashed local capture files; this browser-storage copy omits their duplicate raw payloads.
